quote: Most of them are Saivites, and a few are Lingayats.
note: Temple priests; legend that Sankaracharya appointed Tamil Brahmans to serve Saiva shrines.

quote: The Smarta Brahmans officiate as their priests at birth, marriage, and death ceremonies.
note: Priests only are Smarta; caste itself Saivite.

quote: The name for Pandaram managers of temples, e.g., at Tiruvadudurai in Tanjore and Mailam in South Arcot.
The Telagas are Vaishnavites, and have Brahmans for their priests.
note: Brahman guru, branded at his hands.

quote: Most of the Tellis are Paramarthos, and follow the Chaitanya form of Vaishnavism
but some are Smartas, and all worship Takuranis (village deities).

caste_std: Tigala / Tamil Smarta Brahmans in Mysore
quote: the Canarese Madhva Brahmans speak of Tamil Smarta Brahmans as Tigalaru.
note: Naming only: Kanarese Madhvas call Tamil Smartas Tigalaru. Tigala caste itself (Palli emigrants) has no sect here.

quote: Both sections are Saivites, in the sense that they abstain from flesh and fish.
note: Kumbakonam Vellalas have an 'Annamala matam' as a temple/institution; headman in Periyakulam, Madura.

quote: They are generally Vaishnavites, wear the sacred thread, and have for their priests Vaishnava Brahmans or Satanis.
The bridegroom makes a namam (Vaishnavite sect mark), or places vibhuti (sacred ashes) on the twelve posts of the pandal
note: Inferred from rites; no explicit sect stated.

quote: Most of them are Vaishnavites, some of whom employ Brahman priests, but the majority of them are guided by gurus of their own, called Kodangi Nayakkan.
followers of the Ramanuja faith
He is said to be a Lingayat.
The Unnis are all Smartas, but a partiality for Bhadrakali is manifested by the Tiyattunnis and Brahmanis.
note: Social matters supervised by Nambutiris. No maṭha. Note: 'Smartas' here is a sect/caste label.

quote: They profess to be Saivites and Vaishnavites, but practically worship village deities
note: Vaishnava Brahman gurus brand the Vaishnavites.

quote: The Valluvans include in their ranks both Vaishnavites and Saivites.
note: Priests in some places Vellala Pandarams; majority of Saivites wear the lingam.

quote: Their spiritual guru is the head of the Kumbakonam math.
note: Stuart quotation; said to have come from Goa; 'Vaisya Brahmans'. Kumbakonam math presumably the Śaṅkara (Kāmakoṭi) seat, but the text does not specify.

quote: They are Saivites. They have their own priests, who are called Panditars.
They profess to be Saivites in the southern districts, and Vaishnavites in the north.
The Variyars are to Saivite temples what the Pisharatis are to Vaishnavite temples.
Each division contains both Vaishnavites and Saivites
note: Pandarams, Thambirans owning matams belong to the Sozhia section; no pitha named.

quote: They are Lingayats, and are called Vipravinodi because they perform acrobatic feats before Vipras, or Brahmans.
They are Lingayats, but do not, as a rule, wear the lingam
note: Attached to Saivite temples; legendary Lingayat mutt Basavanna Mandiram.

quote: The Yanadis, like Hindus, wear sect marks, and are even divided into Vaishnavites and Saivites.
